question: Can the K-selection strategy reliably DETECT K != 1 (multiple tactics) on multi-solution expert trajectories?
setup: Synthetic multi-modal trajectories with KNOWN true K (2 or 3 injected tactic modes, plus a single-modal K=1 control). Discovery = per-window SequenceMixture; trajectory-level majority vote. Old rule = 1-SE (hardcoded se + complexity penalty); New rule = best-restart selection loss + empty-cluster disqualify + greedy relative-improvement across K.
key_fixes: (1) posterior-collapse / empty-cluster: single-restart K=3 collapsed to occupancy [0,2112,858] making K=3 look worse than K=2; fixed by BEST-RESTART over seeds + disqualify any K with an empty cluster (occupancy<1 => loss=inf).

(2) unreliable K rule: old 1-SE with hardcoded se=0.001 + complexity penalty crushed true structure into K=1; new rule uses best-seed selection loss + greedy relative improvement (accept larger K only if clearly better), with empty-cluster disqualification.
(3) evaluation must be permutation-free: cluster ids are arbitrary; report best-permutation trajectory-tactic match.
conclusion: With the fixes, K != 1 IS reliably detectable (K=2 and K=3 both recovered; single-modal control stays at K=1, no false positive), and trajectory-level tactic identity is recovered perfectly (match 1.00). The old rule was NOT the main bottleneck alone - posterior collapse of the mixture was equally important.
